thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: Armo, an autonomous retail-store robot and analytics/promotions platform intended to move goods for shelf replenishment, support inventory operations and interact with shoppers. The company states that customers need the outcome addressed by its described product; precise quantified pain was not independently verified. Verified current scope: robot body/device and store workflow; named retail deployments and KPI estimates are company-controlled. Stated ambition: unclear. Public evidence supports responsibility for hardware, robot body and models/policies; supports only partial/shared responsibility for end effectors/tooling and integration; does not establish responsibility for simulation/training, commissioning/qualification, remote operations, ongoing support/maintenance and hardware financing/RaaS. Overall integration responsibility is classified as shared. Commercial evidence: 2_first_party_deployment_claim; technical evidence: 3_vendor_documented. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Partial integration comparator: public evidence supports a company role in integration or qualification, but responsibility is shared with a customer, OEM or partner. Commercial evidence is 2_first_party_deployment_claim; whole-workflow prime responsibility is not established.
